institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 23, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2016. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published December 2017.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin.
method: Vitek 2 YST antifungal susceptibility cards (bioMerieux, France) and E test, repeat isolates excluded; cumulative antibiogram per CLSI M39-A (printed "CLSI M-39A Vol. 22, No. 8; 2002 (global consensus guidelines)"); interpreted as per CLSI M27-S4 (2012), and the C. albicans breakpoints were used where no species-specific breakpoints are available; amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml.

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then cut into two halves with the species column kept on both: no differences. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 23, No. 2 (published December 2017), data January to December 2016, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2016)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". Footnotes as in 2015: "- = Not done"; NA "Guidelines not available"; CLSI M27S4 2012 with the C. albicans breakpoints where no species-specific breakpoints are available (noted on the cells concerned); C. glabrata fluconazole and voriconazole print "NA" and the # footnote (no susceptible category for fluconazole, no voriconazole breakpoints) is printed although the row carries no mark (left out); * and ** as before (Vitek 2 YST cards, E test, repeat isolates excluded, CLSI M39-A 2002; amphotericin B as isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml). No flucytosine column. Every species in the table has an organism key. Organism names: "C. lusitainiae" is recorded as Candida lusitaniae and "Kodaemia ohmerii" as Kodamaea ohmeri. The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "December-2017"). The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 58 cells and 12 n: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: C. auris is printed alone ("C.auris (34)"), so recording it under C. auris is right; C. glabrata fluconazole and voriconazole "NA" (no # mark on the row, # footnote printed) left out with the right note; no species without a key; breakpoints "CLSI M27-S4 (2012)" matches the page. The intrinsic cell C. krusei fluconazole 0 is printed that way.
